blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.8
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.8

blocks.text: जाग्रद्द्वितीयकरः
blocks.directed: [slowly] जाग्रद्द्वितीयकरः

blocks.text: Jāgrad dvitīyakaraḥ.
blocks.directed: Jāgrad dvitīyakaraḥ.

blocks.text: The awakened yogi sees the apparently second reality — the world — as a ray of their own consciousness.
blocks.directed: The awakened yogi sees the apparently second reality — the world — as a ray of their own consciousness.

blocks.text: The Entire Universe Is Apparently Your Own Bloody Sunshine.
blocks.directed: The Entire Universe Is Apparently Your Own Bloody Sunshine.

blocks.text: Now this is a fascinating sūtra.
blocks.directed: Now this is a fascinating sūtra.

blocks.text: Because taken without commentary, it’s fairly cryptic.
blocks.directed: Because taken without commentary, it’s fairly cryptic.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack it.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack it.

blocks.text: Jāgrat — awake, waking, watchful.
blocks.directed: Jāgrat — awake, waking, watchful.

blocks.text: Dvitīya — second, another.
blocks.directed: Dvitīya — second, another.

blocks.text: Kara — ray, beam, radiance.
blocks.directed: Kara — ray, beam, radiance.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja provides the crucial interpretation.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja provides the crucial interpretation.

blocks.text: The yogi established in innate knowledge remains awake in the deeper sense of being established in recognition.
blocks.directed: The yogi established in innate knowledge remains awake in the deeper sense of being established in recognition.

blocks.text: And the apparently second reality — the world of objects — appears as the radiance of consciousness.
blocks.directed: And the apparently second reality — the world of objects — appears as the radiance of consciousness.

blocks.text: This is the relationship between:
blocks.directed: [short pause] This is the relationship between:

blocks.text: Aham — I.
blocks.directed: Aham — I.

blocks.text: And:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And:

blocks.text: Idam — this.
blocks.directed: Idam — this.

blocks.text: Now we’ve encountered these before, but this is where their significance becomes particularly beautiful.
blocks.directed: Now we’ve encountered these before, but this is where their significance becomes particularly beautiful.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, experience seems to involve two fundamentally separate realities.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, experience seems to involve two fundamentally separate realities.

blocks.text: There’s me.
blocks.directed: There’s me.

blocks.text: And there’s everything else.
blocks.directed: And there’s everything else.

blocks.text: I look at a tree.
blocks.directed: I look at a tree.

blocks.text: The tree is over there.
blocks.directed: The tree is over there.

blocks.text: I am over here.
blocks.directed: I am over here.

blocks.text: Subject and object.
blocks.directed: Subject and object.

blocks.text: But within the Trika metaphysical system, the relationship is more subtle.
blocks.directed: But within the Trika metaphysical system, the relationship is more subtle.

blocks.text: The supreme Aham, universal I-consciousness, possesses the freedom to manifest the entire domain of Idam, this-ness or objectivity.
blocks.directed: The supreme Aham, universal I-consciousness, possesses the freedom to manifest the entire domain of Idam, this-ness or objectivity.

blocks.text: The world is not some entirely independent substance standing opposite Śiva.
blocks.directed: The world is not some entirely independent substance standing opposite Śiva.

blocks.text: It is the manifestation of Śiva’s own Śakti.
blocks.directed: It is the manifestation of Śiva’s own Śakti.

blocks.text: So what happens when the yogi recognises this?
blocks.directed: So what happens when the yogi recognises this?

blocks.text: The objects don’t necessarily disappear.
blocks.directed: The objects don’t necessarily disappear.

blocks.text: The tree is still there.
blocks.directed: The tree is still there.

blocks.text: The river still flows.
blocks.directed: The river still flows.

blocks.text: The mountains remain.
blocks.directed: The mountains remain.

blocks.text: The mosquitoes still apparently regard your ankles as a charitable buffet.
blocks.directed: The mosquitoes still apparently regard your ankles as a charitable buffet.

blocks.text: But the ontological understanding of these appearances is transformed.
blocks.directed: But the ontological understanding of these appearances is transformed.

blocks.text: They’re recognised as expressions of the same consciousness whose nature has become apparent.
blocks.directed: They’re recognised as expressions of the same consciousness whose nature has become apparent.

blocks.text: Now think of the sun.
blocks.directed: Now think of the sun.

blocks.text: The sun gives off light.
blocks.directed: The sun gives off light.

blocks.text: Its rays illuminate the world.
blocks.directed: Its rays illuminate the world.

blocks.text: And although the rays are distinguishable in their manifestations, they are not some fundamentally foreign power independent of their source.
blocks.directed: And although the rays are distinguishable in their manifestations, they are not some fundamentally foreign power independent of their source.

blocks.text: This is the metaphor Vasugupta uses.
blocks.directed: This is the metaphor Vasugupta uses.

blocks.text: Kara.
blocks.directed: Kara.

blocks.text: A ray.
blocks.directed: A ray.

blocks.text: The world is the radiance of consciousness.
blocks.directed: The world is the radiance of consciousness.

blocks.text: And this is enormously significant because it means liberation isn’t simply a withdrawal from objectivity.
blocks.directed: And this is enormously significant because it means liberation isn’t simply a withdrawal from objectivity.

blocks.text: It’s a transformation in the recognition of objectivity.
blocks.directed: It’s a transformation in the recognition of objectivity.

blocks.text: You’re not supposed to sit there with your eyes closed forever, desperately trying to avoid the existence of tables.
blocks.directed: You’re not supposed to sit there with your eyes closed forever, desperately trying to avoid the existence of tables.

blocks.text: You’re supposed to recognise the fundamental nature of the reality in which the tables appear.
blocks.directed: You’re supposed to recognise the fundamental nature of the reality in which the tables appear.

blocks.text: The world is no longer encountered as an ultimately alien second reality.
blocks.directed: The world is no longer encountered as an ultimately alien second reality.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja cites the Vijñānabhairava to support this.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja cites the Vijñānabhairava to support this.

blocks.text: He describes the recognition of consciousness in whatever is perceived — including colour and pleasure — and the attainment of fullness through absorption into omnipresent consciousness.
blocks.directed: He describes the recognition of consciousness in whatever is perceived — including colour and pleasure — and the attainment of fullness through absorption into omnipresent consciousness.

blocks.text: He also cites a tantric statement describing the entire world as the powers of Śiva, the possessor of Śakti. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He also cites a tantric statement describing the entire world as the powers of Śiva, the possessor of Śakti. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now let’s consider the philosophical implication.
blocks.directed: Now let’s consider the philosophical implication.

blocks.text: If the world is the radiance of consciousness, then recognition doesn’t have to depend on a privileged sensory object.
blocks.directed: If the world is the radiance of consciousness, then recognition doesn’t have to depend on a privileged sensory object.

blocks.text: You don’t need the perfect sunset.
blocks.directed: You don’t need the perfect sunset.

blocks.text: You don’t need an extraordinary vision.
blocks.directed: You don’t need an extraordinary vision.

blocks.text: You don’t need the Himalayas to appear through the mist while somebody plays a rather moving piece of devotional music.
blocks.directed: You don’t need the Himalayas to appear through the mist while somebody plays a rather moving piece of devotional music.

blocks.text: Lovely though that would be.
blocks.directed: Lovely though that would be.

blocks.text: Any manifestation can become an occasion for recognition.
blocks.directed: Any manifestation can become an occasion for recognition.

blocks.text: A colour.
blocks.directed: A colour.

blocks.text: A sound.
blocks.directed: A sound.

blocks.text: The feeling of movement.
blocks.directed: The feeling of movement.

blocks.text: The appearance of another person.
blocks.directed: The appearance of another person.

blocks.text: The emergence of a thought.
blocks.directed: The emergence of a thought.

blocks.text: Because the essential point is not the particular content.
blocks.directed: Because the essential point is not the particular content.

blocks.text: It’s the conscious reality through which the content becomes manifest.
blocks.directed: It’s the conscious reality through which the content becomes manifest.

blocks.text: And here we arrive at something particularly elegant.
blocks.directed: And here we arrive at something particularly elegant.

blocks.text: In the first book, Vasugupta said:
blocks.directed: [short pause] In the first book, Vasugupta said:

blocks.text: दृश्यं शरीरम्।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] दृश्यं शरीरम्।.

blocks.text: Dṛśyaṃ śarīram.
blocks.directed: Dṛśyaṃ śarīram.

blocks.text: The seen is the body.
blocks.directed: The seen is the body.

blocks.text: Now he’s explaining the same expanded recognition through the imagery of light.
blocks.directed: Now he’s explaining the same expanded recognition through the imagery of light.

blocks.text: The world is the yogi’s radiance.
blocks.directed: The world is the yogi’s radiance.

blocks.text: The apparent second is not ultimately separate from the first.
blocks.directed: The apparent second is not ultimately separate from the first.

blocks.text: And therefore the liberated yogi can remain awake in the midst of ordinary experience.
blocks.directed: And therefore the liberated yogi can remain awake in the midst of ordinary experience.

blocks.text: Not because they’ve stopped perceiving differences.
blocks.directed: Not because they’ve stopped perceiving differences.

blocks.text: But because the differences no longer conceal their conscious source.
blocks.directed: But because the differences no longer conceal their conscious source.

blocks.text: And that brings us to a revelation so magnificent that Vasugupta apparently decides to abandon metaphysical exposition and become a theatre critic.
blocks.directed: And that brings us to a revelation so magnificent that Vasugupta apparently decides to abandon metaphysical exposition and become a theatre critic.
